title: psa_portal_token — a table storing an (encrypted) PSA portal access token — was created after the 000003 blanket RLS grant and has never had RLS enabled

evidence.claim: psa_portal_token is created in 000016 with no ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY / CREATE POLICY anywhere in any of the 25 migrations.
evidence.output:
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS psa_portal_token (
    id           INTEGER PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT 1,
    access_token TEXT NOT NULL,
    expires_at   TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL,
    updated_at   TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
    CONSTRAINT psa_portal_token_singleton CHECK (id = 1)
);

evidence.claim: No RLS statement for this table exists in any migration (grep across all 25 .up.sql files, filtered to this table name, is empty).
evidence.command: grep -n 'ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY\|CREATE POLICY' internal/adapters/storage/postgres/migrations/*.up.sql | grep -w psa_portal_token
evidence.output: (no output — zero matches)

evidence.claim: db-map.json's own scout-computed rls_status for this table agrees: none, and dates its creation as after the 000003 blanket pass.
evidence.output: grep -n 'ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY\|CREATE POLICY' internal/adapters/storage/postgres/migrations/*.up.sql | grep -w psa_portal_token | rls_status=none (no ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY and no CREATE POLICY for this table in any of the 25 migrations -- created after 000003's blanket grant and never retrofitted)

evidence.claim: The stored value is application-layer encrypted before insert and decrypted only in Go (PSAPortalTokenStore uses crypto.Encryptor), so a PostgREST reader without the app's ENCRYPTION_KEY gets ciphertext, not the plaintext PSA token — this narrows but does not eliminate the exposure (ciphertext + ability to overwrite/delete the singleton row and observe expires_at are still exposed).
evidence.output:
internal/adapters/storage/postgres/psa_portal_token_store.go:44:	tok, err := s.enc.Decrypt(enc)
internal/adapters/storage/postgres/psa_portal_token_store.go:53:	enc, err := s.enc.Encrypt(token)

evidence.claim: The table is live (7 references), so this is a live-table gap, not a stale record about a dropped object.
evidence.output: {"external_refs": 7, "ref_sites": ["internal/adapters/storage/postgres/psa_portal_token_store.go:58 INSERT INTO psa_portal_token"]}

searched_universe: internal/adapters/storage/postgres/migrations/*.up.sql (all 25 migrations), cross-checked against docs/audit/maps/db-map.json rls_policy records and table records
exclusions: Verifying the actual production PostgREST/anon-role grant behavior on Supabase requires DB access, which this audit forbids; this finding rests on the migration-file evidence that RLS was never enabled, which is provable from source alone regardless of the exact grant model in place.
proposed_fix: Add a new migration enabling RLS and a service-role-bypass policy for psa_portal_token, following the exact pattern used in 000003 (ALTER TABLE ... ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY; CREATE POLICY "service role bypass" ON ... USING (true) WITH CHECK (true);). Consider also auditing whether this table needs to exist in the public Supabase project at all, given it holds token material even if encrypted.
acceptance_criteria: A new migration's .up.sql contains 'ALTER TABLE public.psa_portal_token ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;' and a CREATE POLICY statement for it; its .down.sql reverses both.
grep -n 'ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY\|CREATE POLICY' internal/adapters/storage/postgres/migrations/*.up.sql | grep -w psa_portal_token now returns two lines.
go test ./... passes (migrations apply cleanly against a local Postgres).

title: psa_campaign_push_queue has no RLS, and the harvester's DrainPushQueue trusts the DB's status column alone — an unauthenticated PostgREST write of a forged 'approved' row would be pushed live to the PSA portal

evidence.claim: psa_campaign_push_queue is created in 000018 with no ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY / CREATE POLICY anywhere in any of the 25 migrations.
evidence.command: grep -n 'ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY\|CREATE POLICY' internal/adapters/storage/postgres/migrations/*.up.sql | grep -w psa_campaign_push_queue
evidence.output: (no output — zero matches)

evidence.claim: DrainPushQueue's only gate before pushing a row live to PSA is the DB row's own status column ('approved'); there is no additional application-level signature or re-authorization check at drain time.
evidence.output: internal/adapters/storage/postgres/psa_campaign_push_queue_store.go:88:		 WHERE id = $1 AND status = 'approved'

evidence.claim: The table is heavily live (21 references) and holds a human-approval workflow (requested_by/approved_by/proposed_diff/status), so an RLS gap here is a write-path integrity issue, not just a read-confidentiality one.

exclusions: Whether Supabase's default anon/authenticated schema grants actually reach this table in the live project is unverifiable without DB access (out of scope); the finding is based on the absence of any RLS statement in the migration source.
proposed_fix: Add RLS (ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY + service-role-bypass policy, matching 000003's pattern) for psa_campaign_push_queue in a new migration. Treat this one ahead of the others in DBSCHEMA-003 given the write-integrity consequence (forged approval rows reaching the live PSA portal).
acceptance_criteria: A new migration's .up.sql enables RLS and adds a policy for psa_campaign_push_queue; .down.sql reverses it.
grep -n 'ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY\|CREATE POLICY' internal/adapters/storage/postgres/migrations/*.up.sql | grep -w psa_campaign_push_queue now returns two lines.

title: docs/SCHEMA.md still cites pre-cutover SQLite migration numbers (up to 000051) that have no corresponding file in this repo's 25-migration Postgres history, making most of its 'Added: migration NNNNN' provenance notes unverifiable or actively misleading

evidence.claim: docs/SCHEMA.md cites migration numbers up to 000051, but the repo's Postgres migration set (post-SQLite-cutover) only goes up to 000025.
evidence.command: grep -oE 'migration 0000[0-9][0-9]' docs/SCHEMA.md | sort -u | tail -5; echo ---; ls internal/adapters/storage/postgres/migrations/*.up.sql | wc -l
evidence.output:
migration 000048
migration 000049
migration 000050
migration 000051
---
25

evidence.claim: CLAUDE.md documents that 000001_initial_schema 'represents the final-state schema after cutover from SQLite' — i.e. the current 25 migrations are a fresh Postgres history, and any doc citation above 000025 necessarily refers to the old, now-collapsed SQLite migration sequence, not a file that exists in this repo.
evidence.output:
Migration files: `internal/adapters/storage/postgres/migrations/`. `000001_initial_schema`
represents the final-state schema after cutover from SQLite; subsequent migrations are
incremental ...

evidence.claim: The overlap is not merely historical trivia: some SCHEMA.md citations in the 000001-000025 range collide with real, different current migrations (see DBSCHEMA-007, where 'migration 000017' is cited for a table actually created by current migration 000018), so a reader cannot tell from the document alone which 'migration NNNNN' citations are pre-cutover artifacts and which refer to a real file in this repo.

searched_universe: docs/SCHEMA.md (all 'migration 0000NN' citations, ~100 occurrences) vs internal/adapters/storage/postgres/migrations/*.up.sql (25 files) and CLAUDE.md's description of the SQLite cutover
exclusions: This finding does not itself enumerate which of the ~100 citations are individually wrong versus merely pre-cutover-but-coincidentally-harmless; DBSCHEMA-006 and DBSCHEMA-007 are the two concretely-verified instances found during this pass. A full doc rewrite is needed to resolve the rest, which is why this is filed as its own (larger-effort) finding rather than folded into those two.
proposed_fix: Rewrite docs/SCHEMA.md's per-table provenance notes to cite only the current 25-migration Postgres history (internal/adapters/storage/postgres/migrations/000001..000025), removing or clearly marking as historical any citation above 000025. Tables entirely defined in 000001_initial_schema should say so rather than citing a pre-cutover number.
acceptance_criteria: grep -oE 'migration 0000[0-9][0-9]' docs/SCHEMA.md, when sorted, has no value greater than 000025.
